validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE/STATUS/LENGTH confirmed high-tier. This is the real, publicly prominent Barauni-Guwahati Natural Gas Pipeline (BGPL), a GAIL project under the Pradhan Mantri Urja Ganga umbrella, inaugurated by PM Modi on 2024-03-09 and connecting Bihar/West Bengal/Assam to the National Gas Grid for the first time. Independently corroborated by: GAIL's own press release (gailonline.com, 2024-04-05, re a CIDC award for the project, states '718 km long pipeline' and 'BGPL' project name), Business Standard (2024-03-08, quoting a GAIL executing-company official), Indian Infrastructure trade press (2024-03-15), CGDIndia (the sheet's existing cited ref, 2024-03-11), and PNGRB's own regulatory register (2026-05-31 NGPL-MIS-Report.pdf, 'PARTIALLY COMMISSIONED COMMON CARRIER PIPELINE' table, row 7: 'Jagdishpur-Haldia-Bokaro Dhamra-Paradip-Barauni-Guwahati', entity GAIL, states 'UP,BR,JH,WB,OD & AS' — confirmed by local pdftotext read; url_verifier gives a documented false negative on this large PDF, token 'Guwahati' does appear on the printed page in a line-wrapped cell that pdftotext renders on the following line). Length 718 km is repeated verbatim and consistently across every source above (GEM's 718.00 km matches). Status=operating and StartYear1=2024 match the March 2024 inauguration. Fuel=Gas and PipelineType=transmission are correct (national-grid trunk transmission line). No existence, classification, or length concern.

validity.researcher_notes: Owner1 = 'Assam Gas Co Ltd' 100% appears WRONG. Every independent source that names an owner/executor names GAIL (India) Limited, not Assam Gas Company Ltd (AGCL): GAIL's own press release ('its Barauni-Guwahati Natural Gas Pipeline project (BGPL)'/'GAIL as a major gas pipeline operator'), Business Standard ('a top official of the executing company, GAIL (India) Ltd'), Indian Infrastructure ('developed by GAIL (India) Limited'), and PNGRB's regulatory register itself, which lists the combined authorized asset's entity as 'GAIL' (row 7, PARTIALLY COMMISSIONED table). I could not find any source naming AGCL as owner/builder of BGPL specifically. AGCL DOES appear in this dataset elsewhere and legitimately — it is the entity of record for the separate 'Assam Natural Gas Pipeline' (105 km, OPERATIONAL table row 17 of the same PNGRB register) and for the roster's own P0906 'Assam Regional Gas Network' — so the likely mechanism of the error is a mix-up between AGCL's Assam-focused gas assets and this much larger GAIL national-grid trunk line that also happens to terminate in Assam. One historical wiki citation is a 2017 PNGRB Expression-of-Interest PDF titled to AGCL ('EOI-NG_AGCL.pdf', for the earlier-named 'Barauni-Bongaigaon-Guwahati' concept) — that document is a scanned image PDF I could not OCR, so I can't rule out an early AGCL role in a since-superseded EOI process, but the pipeline that was actually built, inaugurated, and now operates under this name and length is unambiguously GAIL's, per four independent 2024 sources plus the regulator's own register.

Route to Update; do not overwrite blind since the sheet number may instead reflect a since-superseded design/authorised figure. Do not fill.
validity.researcher_notes: Capacity [ref] is currently MISSING_REF with value 4.38 bcm/y (equivalent to ~12.0 MMSCMD at the India-standard MMSCMD*365/1000 conversion the orchestrator flagged as GEM's likely derivation method). I could not find any source supporting a ~12 MMSCMD design/authorised capacity for BGPL specifically. Instead, Business Standard (2024-03-08), quoting a GAIL/executing-company official directly, states: 'The 24-inch diameter pipeline has the capacity to transport around 2.5 MMSCMD of natural gas' — that's ~0.91 bcm/y, materially lower than the sheet's 4.38. The same '24-inch / 2.5 MMSCMD' phrasing also surfaced verbatim in wire-syndicated coverage (e.g. the ANI headline text, which 403'd on direct fetch but appeared in search snippets), so this looks like ONE originating quote reprinted across outlets rather than two independently-sourced figures — tier medium, not high, on that basis. Separately, PNGRB's current register (2026-05-31 edition) does not itemise BGPL alone; it reports the WHOLE combined 'Jagdishpur-Haldia-Bokaro Dhamra-Paradip-Barauni-Guwahati' system (3,546 km) at an authorised/determined capacity of 23.0 MMSCMD (~8.4 bcm/y) with 11.5 MMSCMD (50%) utilisation — that figure covers the entire multi-thousand-km system, not just the 718 km Barauni-Guwahati leg, so it is not directly comparable and I have not used it to adjudicate. Net: the sheet's 4.38 bcm/y does not match the one segment-specific figure I could find (2.5 MMSCMD), and I do not have a second independent confirmation of either number, so I am flagging rather than filling.
